sourcedFrom: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed (UNDATED — no year is printed in the book)
cleanIntro: ⛔ On this rifle the safety cannot be applied unless the hammer is cocked, and Serbu repeat that note beside every single unload and cleaning instruction in the book. So the first thing to learn is the order: hammer cocked, safety to SAFE, magazine out, then look in the chamber. The strip needs a punch or a dummy round and nothing else, it comes apart into bolt, buttpad, recoil spring and trigger/magazine housing — and the chamber goes back DRY.

steps.title: Safety to SAFE — and it will not go there unless the hammer is cocked
steps.action: Put the safety selector on SAFE first. If it will not move, the hammer is not cocked; cock it and try again. Serbu print that note beside every procedure in the book, which tells you how often people meet it and assume the safety is broken.
steps.aside: Note: If hammer is not cocked, safety selector can not be placed on SAFE.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — UNLOADING

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back, LOOK into the receiver
steps.action: Keep your finger off the trigger, press the magazine catch and take the magazine out. Then pull the bolt handle rearward and look into the receiver to see the chamber is empty. Looking is the instruction — not feeling the magazine well and assuming.
steps.quote: Pull bolt handle (D) rearward and look into receiver to verify that there is no ammunition in chamber (E).
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — UNLOADING

steps.title: Eye protection on, and let it COOL first
steps.action: Serbu ask for eye protection during disassembly and for the components to be allowed to cool after firing. Both are worth taking literally on a .50: there are captive springs in this strip, and a barrel that has just been fired holds enough heat to burn through a moment's inattention.
steps.caution: CAUTION - Allow components to cool after ﬁring.
steps.quote: WARNING - Wear eye protection while disassembling ﬁrearm.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt handle out against the recoil spring
steps.action: Pull the bolt back and press the bolt handle retaining plunger in with a dummy round or a punch. Hold back against the recoil spring while you do it, and take the bolt handle out. The hold is the point — the spring is what pushes the parts out of your hand if you let go at the wrong moment.
steps.aside: round or punch. Hold back against recoil spring and remove bolt handle (B).
steps.quote: Pull bolt back and depress bolt handle retaining plunger (A) with a dummy
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — REMOVE BOLT

steps.title: Takedown pin out while you HOLD the buttpad
steps.action: Push the takedown pin in with the dummy round or punch and pull it out — but keep hold of the buttpad while you do. Behind it is the recoil spring, and the buttpad is the only thing containing it.
steps.quote: Push in on takedown pin (C) with a dummy round or punch. While holding ontobuttpad (D) remove pin.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt apart: cam pin through the access hole, then the extractor
steps.action: Push the bolt head into the bolt carrier until the cam pin lines up with the round access hole, take the cam pin out and the bolt head follows. Then the extractor: press it in, depress the extractor plunger with a small punch, and slide the extractor past the plunger. ⛔ Expect the plunger and its spring to leave the bolt head the moment the extractor is clear — Serbu say so, and it is a small spring on a big bench.
steps.caution: Note: Plunger is under pressure. Plunger and spring will release from bolt head once extractor has been removed.
steps.quote: Push bolt head (D) into bolt carrier (E) until cam pin (F) lines up with round access hole. Remove cam pin and bolt head.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Trigger/magazine housing on two pins — and stop there
steps.action: Push in on the two pins and the trigger/magazine housing assembly comes out as a unit. ⛔ That is the end of the published strip. Serbu repeat the limit twice on the same page and give a phone number for parts and technical information rather than a further procedure.
steps.caution: WARNING - Do not disassemble the ﬁrearm any further than instructed in this manual.
steps.quote: Push in on pins (A and C). Remove trigger/magazine housing assembly (B).
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — REMOVE TRIGGER/MAGAZINE HOUSING ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Barrel with a patch on a rod, until the patch stays clean
steps.action: Magazine out, rifle verified empty, safety on SAFE. Then a cotton patch on a cleaning rod, moistened with cleaning solution, repeated with clean patches until they come out clean. Serbu sell a .50 BMG-specific kit and say to follow its instructions if you have it.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel with a cotton patch attached to a cleaning rod. Moisten the patch with cleaning solution.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE BARREL

steps.title: ⛔ The chamber gets a dry patch last, and NO oil
steps.action: Solvent and a chamber brush, worked through several times, then clean patches until one stays clean — and finally a DRY patch. ⛔ The chamber is not oiled. An oiled .50 chamber does not let the case grip the walls, and the bolt takes thrust it was not meant to take.
steps.quote: After cleaning, run a dry patch through the chamber. Do not oil the chamber.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE CHAMBER

steps.title: Trigger housing: air and a cloth, grease only on hammer and sear
steps.action: Wipe the trigger/magazine housing with a clean cloth, then a lightly oiled one; compressed air is useful in here and eye protection is not optional when you use it. ⛔ Grease goes on the hammer and the trigger sear surfaces and nowhere else in the mechanism.
steps.quote: Never apply grease to the trigger mechanism except to the hammer and trigger sear surfaces.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE TRIGGER/MAGAZINE HOUSING

steps.title: Bolt carrier group and the carrier channel
steps.action: Wipe every surface of the bolt carrier group with a clean cloth and follow with a lightly oiled one, and clear debris off the bolt, firing pin, retaining pin, cam pin and extractor. Then wipe the debris out of the bolt carrier channel in the receiver — the place it all ends up.
steps.aside: Wipe any debris from the bolt carrier channel.
steps.quote: Wipe any debris from the bolt, ﬁring pin, retaining pin, cam pin and extractor.
steps.cite: Serbu BFG-50A Rifle Operator's Manual — BFG50AManual (the file Serbu publishes at serbu.com/content/); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE BOLT CARRIER GROUP

deepAbsentReason: The strip in the guided clean above IS Serbu's whole published procedure, all the way down to the extractor plunger — bolt out, bolt apart, trigger/magazine housing off. There is nothing deeper because Serbu draw the line there in as many words, twice on the same page: "Do not disassemble the firearm any further than instructed in this manual" and "Do not modify or alter any part of the firearm. Contact Serbu Firearms at (813) 243-8899 for replacement parts and/or technical information." ⚠ That is a limit backed by a phone number rather than by a procedure, which is the maker saying the next operation is theirs. Nothing deeper is presented here and none has been invented.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Cotton patch on a rod with cleaning solution
Repeated with clean patches until the patch stays clean
A .50 BMG-specific kit is available from Serbu; follow its instructions if used

cleaning.name: ⛔ CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent and a chamber brush, several passes
Clean patches until one stays clean
A DRY patch last — the chamber is NEVER oiled

cleaning.name: TRIGGER / MAGAZINE HOUSING
tasks: Clean cloth, then a lightly oiled cloth
Compressed air is useful — eye protection when using it
⛔ Grease ONLY on the hammer and trigger sear surfaces

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: All surfaces wiped, then a lightly oiled cloth
Debris off bolt, firing pin, retaining pin, cam pin and extractor

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & INTERVAL
tasks: Metal surfaces wiped, then lightly oiled
Cleaned as soon as possible after firing, and if the rifle gets wet
Unfired: once or twice a year in a temperate climate, up to weekly in a tropical one

reassembly: Trigger/magazine housing back in on its two pins.
Extractor, plunger and spring into the bolt head, then the bolt head into the carrier and the cam pin home.
Recoil spring and buttpad in together, takedown pin pushed home while the buttpad is held.
Bolt handle in against recoil-spring pressure until the retaining plunger clicks.
⛔ Chamber checked DRY, not oiled, before any ammunition comes near it.
fncheck: Back together and empty: cock the hammer and confirm the safety selector will now go to SAFE — if it will not, the hammer is not cocked, which is the same note Serbu print beside every procedure. Work the bolt by hand and let the recoil spring close it. Check the magazine seats and drops on the catch, and look through the chamber once more.
